public_domain_references.asv: When it goeth well with the righteous, the city rejoiceth; And when the wicked perish, there is shouting.
public_domain_references.kjv: When it goeth well with the righteous, the city rejoiceth: and when the wicked perish, [there is] shouting.
public_domain_references.brenton: In the prosperity of righteous men a city prospers:

pob.text: By the blessing of the upright a city is exalted[b][a], but by the mouth of the wicked it is torn down.

spob.text: A city prospers through the blessing of upright people,[a] but wicked people tear it down with their words.

public_domain_references.bsb: By the blessing of the upright a city is built up, but by the mouth of the wicked it is torn down.
public_domain_references.web: By the blessing of the upright, the city is exalted, but it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.
public_domain_references.asv: By the blessing of the upright the city is exalted; But it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.
public_domain_references.kjv: By the blessing of the upright the city is exalted: but it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.
public_domain_references.brenton: but by the mouths of ungodly men it is overthrown.

pob.text: Whoever despises his neighbor lacks sense[c][b][a], but a man of understanding keeps silent.

spob.text: Whoever treats his neighbor with contempt has no sense. But a man[a] with understanding keeps silent.

public_domain_references.web: One who despises his neighbor is void of wisdom, but a man of understanding holds his peace.
public_domain_references.asv: He that despiseth his neighbor is void of wisdom; But a man of understanding holdeth his peace.
public_domain_references.kjv: He that is void of wisdom despiseth his neighbour: but a man of understanding holdeth his peace.
public_domain_references.brenton: A man void of understanding sneers at [his fellow] citizens: but a sensible man is quiet.

pob.text: A gossip reveals a secret[b][a], but one who is faithful in spirit conceals a matter.

spob.text: A gossip gives away a secret, but someone who is trustworthy in spirit[a] keeps it private.

public_domain_references.bsb: A gossip reveals a secret, but a trustworthy person keeps a confidence.
public_domain_references.web: One who brings gossip betrays a confidence, but one who is of a trustworthy spirit is one who keeps a secret.
public_domain_references.asv: He that goeth about as a tale-bearer revealeth secrets; But he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth a matter.
public_domain_references.kjv: A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.
public_domain_references.brenton: A double-tongued man discloses the [secret] counsels of an assembly: but he that is faithful in spirit conceals matters.

pob.text: Without guidance a people falls[a], but in an abundance of counselors there is deliverance.

spob.text: When a people has no guidance, it falls. But when it has many advisers, there is deliverance.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: For lack of guidance, a nation falls, but with many counselors comes deliverance.
public_domain_references.web: Where there is no wise guidance, the nation falls, but in the multitude of counselors there is victory.
public_domain_references.asv: Where no wise guidance is, the people falleth; But in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.
public_domain_references.kjv: Where no counsel [is], the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors [there is] safety.
public_domain_references.brenton: They that have no guidance fall like leaves: but in much counsel there is safety.

pob.text: He will surely suffer harm who becomes surety for a stranger[b][a], but whoever hates striking hands is secure.

spob.text: Anyone who guarantees a stranger’s obligation is sure to suffer harm, but whoever hates making pledges with a handshake[a] is safe.

public_domain_references.bsb: He who puts up security for a stranger will surely suffer, but the one who hates indebtedness is secure.
public_domain_references.web: He who is collateral for a stranger will suffer for it, but he who refuses pledges of collateral is secure.
public_domain_references.asv: He that is surety for a stranger shall smart for it; But he that hateth suretyship is secure.
public_domain_references.kjv: He that is surety for a stranger shall smart [for it:] and he that hateth suretiship is sure.
public_domain_references.brenton: A bad man does harm wherever he meets a just man: and he hates the sound of safety.

pob.text: A gracious woman obtains honor[a], and ruthless men obtain wealth.

spob.text: A gracious woman gains honor[a], while ruthless men gain wealth.

public_domain_references.bsb: A gracious woman attains honor, but ruthless men gain only wealth.
public_domain_references.web: A gracious woman obtains honor, but violent men obtain riches.
public_domain_references.asv: A gracious woman obtaineth honor; And violent men obtain riches.
public_domain_references.kjv: A gracious woman retaineth honour: and strong [men] retain riches.
public_domain_references.brenton: A gracious wife brings glory to her husband: but a woman hating righteousness is a theme of dishonour. The slothful come to want: but the diligent support themselves with wealth.

pob.text: A kind man benefits himself[a], but a cruel man troubles his own flesh.

spob.text: A kind man does himself good, but a cruel man brings trouble on his own body.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: A kind man benefits himself, but a cruel man brings trouble on himself.
public_domain_references.web: The merciful man does good to his own soul, but he who is cruel troubles his own flesh.
public_domain_references.asv: The merciful man doeth good to his own soul; But he that is cruel troubleth his own flesh.
public_domain_references.kjv: The merciful man doeth good to his own soul: but [he that is] cruel troubleth his own flesh.
public_domain_references.brenton: A merciful man does good to his own soul: but the merciless destroys his own body.

pob.text: A wicked man earns deceptive wages[b][a], but one who sows righteousness receives a true reward.

spob.text: A wicked man earns a reward that proves false, but one who sows righteousness receives a reward that is real and sure.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The wicked man earns an empty wage, but he who sows righteousness reaps a true reward.
public_domain_references.web: Wicked people earn deceitful wages, but one who sows righteousness reaps a sure reward.
public_domain_references.asv: The wicked earneth deceitful wages; But he that soweth righteousness [hath] a sure reward.
public_domain_references.kjv: The wicked worketh a deceitful work: but to him that soweth righteousness [shall be] a sure reward.
public_domain_references.brenton: An ungodly man performs unrighteous works: but the seed of the righteous is a reward of truth.

pob.text: So righteousness leads to life[a], but he who pursues evil, to his own death.

spob.text: So, righteous living leads to life,[a] but whoever keeps pursuing evil brings death on himself.

public_domain_references.bsb: Genuine righteousness leads to life, but the pursuit of evil brings death.
public_domain_references.web: He who is truly righteous gets life. He who pursues evil gets death.
public_domain_references.asv: He that is stedfast in righteousness [shall attain] unto life; And he that pursueth evil [doeth it] to his own death.
public_domain_references.kjv: As righteousness [tendeth] to life: so he that pursueth evil [pursueth it] to his own death.
public_domain_references.brenton: A righteous son is born for life: but the persecution of the ungodly [ends] in death.

pob.text: The crooked in heart are an abomination to Yahweh[b][a], but those blameless in their way are his delight.

spob.text: Yahweh detests people whose hearts are crooked, but he delights in those who live with integrity.

public_domain_references.bsb: The perverse in heart are an abomination to the LORD, but the blameless in their walk are His delight.
public_domain_references.web: Those who are perverse in heart are an abomination to Yahweh, but those whose ways are blameless are his delight.
public_domain_references.asv: They that are perverse in heart are an abomination to Jehovah; But such as are perfect in [their] way are his delight.
public_domain_references.kjv: They that are of a froward heart [are] abomination to the LORD: but [such as are] upright in [their] way [are] his delight.
public_domain_references.brenton: Perverse ways are an abomination to the Lord: but all they that are blameless in their ways are acceptable to him.

pob.text: Hand to hand[a], the evil will not go unpunished, but the offspring of the righteous will escape.

spob.text: Hand to hand,[a] an evil man will not escape punishment, but the descendants of righteous people will escape.

public_domain_references.bsb: Be assured that the wicked will not go unpunished, but the offspring of the righteous will escape.
public_domain_references.web: Most certainly, the evil man will not be unpunished, but the offspring of the righteous will be delivered.
public_domain_references.asv: [Though] hand [join] in hand, the evil man shall not be unpunished; But the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.
public_domain_references.kjv: [Though] hand [join] in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished: but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.
public_domain_references.brenton: He that unjustly strikes hands shall not be unpunished: but he that sows righteousness shall receive a faithful reward.

pob.text: Like a gold ring in a pig’s snout is a beautiful woman who lacks discretion[a].

spob.text: A beautiful woman who has no good sense is like a gold ring in a pig’s snout.

public_domain_references.bsb: Like a gold ring in a pig’s snout is a beautiful woman who lacks discretion.
public_domain_references.web: Like a gold ring in a pig’s snout, is a beautiful woman who lacks discretion.
public_domain_references.asv: [As] a ring of gold in a swine’s snout, [So is] a fair woman that is without discretion.
public_domain_references.kjv: [As] a jewel of gold in a swine’s snout, [so is] a fair woman which is without discretion.
public_domain_references.brenton: As an ornament in a swine's snout, so is beauty to an ill-minded woman.

pob.text: The desire of the righteous is only good[b][a], but the hope of the wicked is wrath.

spob.text: Righteous people desire only what is good, but what wicked people hope for amounts to wrath.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The desire of the righteous leads only to good, but the hope of the wicked brings wrath.

public_domain_references.asv: The desire of the righteous is only good; [But] the expectation of the wicked is wrath.
public_domain_references.kjv: The desire of the righteous [is] only good: [but] the expectation of the wicked [is] wrath.
public_domain_references.brenton: All the desire of the righteous is good: but the hope of the ungodly shall perish.

pob.text: There is one who scatters[a], yet gains still more; and one who withholds more than is right, but only to poverty.

spob.text: One person gives freely, scattering what they have, yet gains even more. Another holds back more than is right,[a] but ends up in poverty.

public_domain_references.bsb: One gives freely, yet gains even more; another withholds what is right, only to become poor.
public_domain_references.web: There is one who scatters, and increases yet more. There is one who withholds more than is appropriate, but gains poverty.
public_domain_references.asv: There is that scattereth, and increaseth yet more; And there is that withholdeth more than is meet, but [it tendeth] only to want.
public_domain_references.kjv: There is that scattereth, and yet increaseth; and [there is] that withholdeth more than is meet, but [it tendeth] to poverty.
public_domain_references.brenton: There are [some] who scatter their own, and make it more: and there are [some] also who gather, [yet] have less.

pob.text: A generous person will be enriched[b][a], and whoever refreshes others will himself be refreshed.

spob.text: Generous people will flourish,[a] and those who refresh others will themselves be refreshed.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: A generous soul will prosper, and he who refreshes others will himself be refreshed.
public_domain_references.web: The liberal soul shall be made fat. He who waters shall be watered also himself.
public_domain_references.asv: The liberal soul shall be made fat; And he that watereth shall be watered also himself.
public_domain_references.kjv: The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.
public_domain_references.brenton: Every sincere soul is blessed: but a passionate man is not graceful.

pob.text: The one who withholds grain—the people curse him[b][a], but blessing is on the head of the one who sells it.

spob.text: People[a] curse anyone who holds back grain, but blessing comes to the one who sells it.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: The people will curse the hoarder of grain, but blessing will crown the one who sells it.
public_domain_references.web: People curse someone who withholds grain, but blessing will be on the head of him who sells it.
public_domain_references.asv: He that withholdeth grain, the people shall curse him; But blessing shall be upon the head of him that selleth it.
public_domain_references.kjv: He that withholdeth corn, the people shall curse him: but blessing [shall be] upon the head of him that selleth [it].
public_domain_references.brenton: May he that hoards corn leave it to the nation: but blessing be on the head of him that gives [it].

pob.text: Whoever diligently seeks good seeks favor[c][b][a], but evil comes to the one who searches for it.

spob.text: Whoever earnestly looks for what is good seeks favor.[a] But evil will come to whoever looks for it.

public_domain_references.bsb: He who searches out good finds favor, but evil will come to him who seeks it.
public_domain_references.web: He who diligently seeks good seeks favor, but he who searches after evil, it shall come to him.

public_domain_references.kjv: He that diligently seeketh good procureth favour: but he that seeketh mischief, it shall come unto him.
public_domain_references.brenton: He that devises good [counsels] seeks good favour: but [as for] him that seeks after evil, [evil] shall overtake him.

pob.text: Whoever trusts in his wealth will fall[a], but the righteous will flourish like leaves.

spob.text: Anyone who trusts in wealth will fall. But righteous people will flourish like leaves.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: He who trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous will thrive like foliage.
public_domain_references.web: He who trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous shall flourish as the green leaf.
public_domain_references.asv: He that trusteth in his riches shall fall; But the righteous shall flourish as the green leaf.
public_domain_references.kjv: He that trusteth in his riches shall fall: but the righteous shall flourish as a branch.
public_domain_references.brenton: He that trusts in wealth shall fall; but he that helps righteous men shall rise.

pob.text: Whoever troubles his own house will inherit wind[b][a], and the fool will be a servant to the wise of heart.

public_domain_references.bsb: He who brings trouble on his house will inherit the wind, and the fool will be servant to the wise of heart.
public_domain_references.web: He who troubles his own house shall inherit the wind. The foolish shall be servant to the wise of heart.
public_domain_references.asv: He that troubleth his own house shall inherit the wind; And the foolish shall be servant to the wise of heart.
public_domain_references.kjv: He that troubleth his own house shall inherit the wind: and the fool [shall be] servant to the wise of heart.
public_domain_references.brenton: He that deals not graciously with his own house shall inherit the wind; and the fool shall be servant to the wise man.

pob.text: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life[a], and he who wins souls is wise.

spob.text: The fruit that righteous people bear is a tree of life, and whoever wins people over[a] is wise.

public_domain_references.bsb: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he who wins souls is wise.
public_domain_references.web: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life. He who is wise wins souls.
public_domain_references.asv: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; And he that is wise winneth souls.
public_domain_references.kjv: The fruit of the righteous [is] a tree of life; and he that winneth souls [is] wise.
public_domain_references.brenton: Out of the fruit of righteousness grows a tree of life; but the souls of transgressors are cut off before their time.

pob.text: Look[a], if the righteous is repaid on earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner.

spob.text: Look: if the righteous receive what is due on earth, how much more will the wicked and the sinner receive what is due![a]

public_domain_references.bsb: If the righteous receive their due on earth, how much more the ungodly and the sinner!
public_domain_references.web: Behold, the righteous shall be repaid on the earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner!
public_domain_references.asv: Behold, the righteous shall be recompensed in the earth; How much more the wicked and the sinner!
public_domain_references.kjv: Behold, the righteous shall be recompensed in the earth: much more the wicked and the sinner.
public_domain_references.brenton: If the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?

pob.text: Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge[a], but he who hates reproof is stupid.

spob.text: Those who love discipline love knowledge, but those who hate correction are stupid.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but he who hates correction is stupid.
public_domain_references.web: Whoever loves correction loves knowledge, but he who hates reproof is stupid.

public_domain_references.kjv: Whoso loveth instruction loveth knowledge: but he that hateth reproof [is] brutish.
public_domain_references.brenton: He that loves instruction loves sense, but he that hates reproofs is a fool.

pob.text: A good man obtains favor from Yahweh[b][a], but a man of schemes he condemns.

spob.text: A good man receives favor from Yahweh, but Yahweh condemns a scheming man.

public_domain_references.bsb: The good man obtains favor from the LORD, but the LORD condemns a man who devises evil.
public_domain_references.web: A good man shall obtain favor from Yahweh, but he will condemn a man of wicked plans.
public_domain_references.asv: A good man shall obtain favor of Jehovah; But a man of wicked devices will he condemn.
public_domain_references.kjv: A good [man] obtaineth favour of the LORD: but a man of wicked devices will he condemn.
public_domain_references.brenton: He that has found favour with the Lord [is made] better; but a transgressor shall be passed over in silence.

pob.text: A man is not established by wickedness[b][a], but the root of the righteous will not be moved.

spob.text: A man cannot gain lasting security through wickedness, but the root of the righteous will not be shaken.

public_domain_references.bsb: A man cannot be established through wickedness, but the righteous cannot be uprooted.
public_domain_references.web: A man shall not be established by wickedness, but the root of the righteous shall not be moved.
public_domain_references.asv: A man shall not be established by wickedness; But the root of the righteous shall not be moved.
public_domain_references.kjv: A man shall not be established by wickedness: but the root of the righteous shall not be moved.
public_domain_references.brenton: A man shall not prosper by wickedness; but the roots of the righteous shall not be taken up.

pob.text: A wife of noble character is her husband's crown[b][a], but one who brings shame is like rot in his bones.

public_domain_references.asv: A worthy woman is the crown of her husband; But she that maketh ashamed is as rottenness in his bones.
public_domain_references.kjv: A virtuous woman [is] a crown to her husband: but she that maketh ashamed [is] as rottenness in his bones.
public_domain_references.brenton: A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband; but as a worm in wood, so a bad woman destroys her husband.

pob.text: The thoughts of the righteous are justice[b][a]; the counsels of the wicked are deceit.

spob.text: Righteous people think in just ways, but wicked people make deceitful plans.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The plans of the righteous are just, but the counsel of the wicked leads to deceit.
public_domain_references.web: The thoughts of the righteous are just, but the advice of the wicked is deceitful.
public_domain_references.asv: The thoughts of the righteous are just; [But] the counsels of the wicked are deceit.
public_domain_references.kjv: The thoughts of the righteous [are] right: [but] the counsels of the wicked [are] deceit.
public_domain_references.brenton: The thoughts of the righteous [are true] judgments; but ungodly men devise deceits.

pob.text: The words of the wicked are an ambush for blood[b][a], but the mouth of the upright delivers them.

spob.text: The words of wicked people are an ambush meant to spill blood, but the mouth of the upright rescues those in danger.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood, but the speech of the upright rescues them.
public_domain_references.web: The words of the wicked are about lying in wait for blood, but the speech of the upright rescues them.
public_domain_references.asv: The words of the wicked are of lying in wait for blood; But the mouth of the upright shall deliver them.
public_domain_references.kjv: The words of the wicked [are] to lie in wait for blood: but the mouth of the upright shall deliver them.
public_domain_references.brenton: The words of ungodly men are crafty; but the mouth of the upright shall deliver them.

pob.text: The wicked are overthrown and are no more[b][a], but the house of the righteous will stand.

spob.text: Wicked people are overthrown and gone, but the house[a] of righteous people will remain standing.

public_domain_references.bsb: The wicked are overthrown and perish, but the house of the righteous will stand.
public_domain_references.web: The wicked are overthrown, and are no more, but the house of the righteous shall stand.
public_domain_references.asv: The wicked are overthrown, and are not; But the house of the righteous shall stand.
public_domain_references.kjv: The wicked are overthrown, and [are] not: but the house of the righteous shall stand.
public_domain_references.brenton: When the ungodly is overthrown, he vanishes away; but the houses of the just remain.

pob.text: A man is praised according to his insight[b][a], but one with a twisted heart will be despised.

spob.text: The praise a man receives reflects his good sense. But a man with a twisted heart[a] will be despised.

public_domain_references.bsb: A man is praised according to his wisdom, but a twisted mind is despised.
public_domain_references.web: A man shall be commended according to his wisdom, but he who has a warped mind shall be despised.
public_domain_references.asv: A man shall be commended according to his wisdom; But he that is of a perverse heart shall be despised.
public_domain_references.kjv: A man shall be commended according to his wisdom: but he that is of a perverse heart shall be despised.
public_domain_references.brenton: The mouth of an understanding [man] is praised by a man; but he that is dull of heart is had in derision.

pob.text: Better is one who is lightly esteemed and has a servant than one who honors himself and lacks bread[a].

spob.text: It is better to be considered unimportant and have a servant than to make yourself important and have no bread.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Better to be lightly esteemed yet have a servant, than to be self-important but lack food.
public_domain_references.web: Better is he who is little known, and has a servant, than he who honors himself and lacks bread.
public_domain_references.asv: Better is he that is lightly esteemed, and hath a servant, Than he that honoreth himself, and lacketh bread.
public_domain_references.kjv: [He that is] despised, and hath a servant, [is] better than he that honoureth himself, and lacketh bread.
public_domain_references.brenton: Better is a man in dishonour serving himself, than one honouring himself and wanting bread.

pob.text: A righteous man knows the life of his animal[a], but the compassion of the wicked is cruel.

spob.text: A righteous man understands his animal’s condition and needs,[a] but the compassion of wicked people is cruel.

public_domain_references.bsb: A righteous man regards the life of his animal, but the tender mercies of the wicked are only cruelty.
public_domain_references.web: A righteous man respects the life of his animal, but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.
public_domain_references.asv: A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast; But the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.
public_domain_references.kjv: A righteous [man] regardeth the life of his beast: but the tender mercies of the wicked [are] cruel.
public_domain_references.brenton: A righteous man has pity for the lives of his cattle; but the bowels of the ungodly are unmerciful.

pob.text: Whoever works his land will have plenty of bread[a], but he who pursues empty things lacks sense.

public_domain_references.brenton: He that tills his own land shall be satisfied with bread; but they that pursue vanities are void of understanding.

pob.text: A wicked man desires the prey of evil men[b][a], but the root of the righteous yields fruit.

spob.text: A wicked man strongly wants what evil men seize, but the righteous are like a root that bears fruit.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The wicked desire the plunder of evil men, but the root of the righteous flourishes.
public_domain_references.web: The wicked desires the plunder of evil men, but the root of the righteous flourishes.
public_domain_references.asv: The wicked desireth the net of evil men; But the root of the righteous yieldeth [fruit].
public_domain_references.kjv: The wicked desireth the net of evil [men:] but the root of the righteous yieldeth [fruit].
public_domain_references.brenton: The desires of the ungodly are evil; but the roots of the godly are firmly set.

pob.text: In the transgression of the lips there is a snare for an evil man[b][a], but the righteous comes out of trouble.

spob.text: A snare lies in an evil man's sinful speech,[a] but the righteous man comes out of trouble.

public_domain_references.bsb: An evil man is trapped by his rebellious speech, but a righteous man escapes from trouble.
public_domain_references.web: An evil man is trapped by sinfulness of lips, but the righteous shall come out of trouble.
public_domain_references.asv: In the transgression of the lips is a snare to the evil man; But the righteous shall come out of trouble.
public_domain_references.kjv: The wicked is snared by the transgression of [his] lips: but the just shall come out of trouble.

public_domain_references.bsb: A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children, but the sinner’s wealth is passed to the righteous.
public_domain_references.web: A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children, but the wealth of the sinner is stored for the righteous.
public_domain_references.asv: A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children; And the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the righteous.
public_domain_references.kjv: A good [man] leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children: and the wealth of the sinner [is] laid up for the just.
public_domain_references.brenton: A good man shall inherit children's children; and the wealth of ungodly men is laid up for the just.

pob.text: The fallow ground of the poor[b][a] yields abundant food, but some are swept away for lack of justice.

spob.text: A poor person’s freshly plowed land produces plenty of food, yet some people are swept away because justice is absent.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Abundant food is in the fallow ground of the poor, but without justice it is swept away.
public_domain_references.web: An abundance of food is in poor people’s fields, but injustice sweeps it away.
public_domain_references.asv: Much food [is in] the tillage of the poor; But there is that is destroyed by reason of injustice.
public_domain_references.kjv: Much food [is in] the tillage of the poor: but there is [that is] destroyed for want of judgment.
public_domain_references.brenton: The righteous shall spend many years in wealth: but the unrighteous shall perish suddenly.

pob.text: Whoever withholds his rod hates his son[b][a], but whoever loves him diligently seeks discipline.

spob.text: Whoever holds back his rod hates his son, but whoever loves his son is diligent in disciplining him.

public_domain_references.bsb: He who spares the rod hates his son, but he who loves him disciplines him diligently.
public_domain_references.web: One who spares the rod hates his son, but one who loves him is careful to discipline him.
public_domain_references.asv: He that spareth his rod hateth his son; But he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes.
public_domain_references.kjv: He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes.
public_domain_references.brenton: He that spares the rod hates his son: but he that loves, carefully chastens [him].

pob.text: A righteous man eats to the satisfaction of his soul[a], but the belly of the wicked lacks.

spob.text: A righteous man eats until he is satisfied,[a] but the belly of the wicked remains hungry.

public_domain_references.bsb: A righteous man eats to his heart’s content, but the stomach of the wicked is empty.
public_domain_references.web: The righteous one eats to the satisfying of his soul, but the belly of the wicked goes hungry.
public_domain_references.asv: The righteous eateth to the satisfying of his soul; But the belly of the wicked shall want.
public_domain_references.kjv: The righteous eateth to the satisfying of his soul: but the belly of the wicked shall want.
public_domain_references.brenton: A just [man] eats and satisfies his soul: but the souls of the ungodly are in want.

pob.text: The wisest of women builds her house[b][a], but a foolish woman tears it down with her own hands.

spob.text: The wisest of women[a] builds her home, but a foolish woman tears it down with her own hands.

public_domain_references.bsb: Every wise woman builds her house, but a foolish one tears it down with her own hands.
public_domain_references.web: Every wise woman builds her house, but the foolish one tears it down with her own hands.
public_domain_references.asv: Every wise woman buildeth her house; But the foolish plucketh it down with her own hands.
public_domain_references.kjv: Every wise woman buildeth her house: but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands.
public_domain_references.brenton: Wise women build houses: but a foolish one digs [hers] down with her hands.

pob.text: Whoever walks in uprightness fears Yahweh[b][a], but the one whose ways are crooked despises him.

spob.text: Whoever walks an upright path fears Yahweh, but whoever follows crooked ways despises him.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: He who walks in uprightness fears the LORD, but the one who is devious in his ways despises Him.
public_domain_references.web: He who walks in his uprightness fears Yahweh, but he who is perverse in his ways despises him.
public_domain_references.asv: He that walketh in his uprightness feareth Jehovah; But he that is perverse in his ways despiseth him.
public_domain_references.kjv: He that walketh in his uprightness feareth the LORD: but [he that is] perverse in his ways despiseth him.
public_domain_references.brenton: He that walks uprightly fears the Lord; but he that is perverse in his ways shall be dishonoured.

pob.text: In the mouth of a fool is a rod of pride[b][a], but the lips of the wise will guard them.

spob.text: A fool’s proud speech is like a rod, but the words of the wise protect those who speak them.[a][b]

public_domain_references.bsb: The proud speech of a fool brings a rod to his back, but the lips of the wise protect them.
public_domain_references.web: The fool’s talk brings a rod to his back, but the lips of the wise protect them.
public_domain_references.asv: In the mouth of the foolish is a rod for [his] pride; But the lips of the wise shall preserve them.
public_domain_references.kjv: In the mouth of the foolish [is] a rod of pride: but the lips of the wise shall preserve them.
public_domain_references.brenton: Out of the mouth of fools [comes] a rod of pride; but the lips of the wise preserve them.

pob.text: Where there are no oxen[a], the manger is clean[b], but abundant crops come by the strength of an ox.

spob.text: When there are no oxen, the feeding trough stays clean. But the strength of an ox brings abundant crops.

public_domain_references.bsb: Where there are no oxen, the manger is empty, but an abundant harvest comes through the strength of the ox.
public_domain_references.web: Where no oxen are, the crib is clean, but much increase is by the strength of the ox.
public_domain_references.asv: Where no oxen are, the crib is clean; But much increase is by the strength of the ox.
public_domain_references.kjv: Where no oxen [are], the crib [is] clean: but much increase [is] by the strength of the ox.
public_domain_references.brenton: Where no oxen are, the cribs are clean; but where there is abundant produce, the strength of the ox is apparent.

pob.text: A faithful witness does not lie[a], but a false witness breathes out lies.

spob.text: A trustworthy witness tells no lies, but a false witness breathes out lies.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: An honest witness does not deceive, but a dishonest witness pours forth lies.
public_domain_references.web: A truthful witness will not lie, but a false witness pours out lies.
public_domain_references.asv: A faithful witness will not lie; But a false witness uttereth lies.
public_domain_references.kjv: A faithful witness will not lie: but a false witness will utter lies.
public_domain_references.brenton: A faithful witness does not lie; but an unjust witness kindles falsehoods.

pob.text: A scoffer seeks wisdom and there is none[b][a], but knowledge comes easily to one who has understanding.

spob.text: A scoffer looks for wisdom but finds none. Knowledge comes easily to someone who understands.

public_domain_references.bsb: A mocker seeks wisdom and finds none, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.
public_domain_references.web: A scoffer seeks wisdom, and doesn’t find it, but knowledge comes easily to a discerning person.
public_domain_references.asv: A scoffer seeketh wisdom, and [findeth it] not; But knowledge is easy unto him that hath understanding.
public_domain_references.kjv: A scorner seeketh wisdom, and [findeth it] not: but knowledge [is] easy unto him that understandeth.
public_domain_references.brenton: Thou shalt seek wisdom with bad men, and shalt not find it; but discretion is easily available with the prudent.

pob.text: Go from the presence of a foolish man[a], for you do not perceive lips of knowledge.

spob.text: Walk away from a foolish man, for you will not find words of knowledge on his lips.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Stay away from a foolish man; you will gain no knowledge from his speech.
public_domain_references.web: Stay away from a foolish man, for you won’t find knowledge on his lips.
public_domain_references.asv: Go into the presence of a foolish man, And thou shalt not perceive [in him] the lips of knowledge.
public_domain_references.kjv: Go from the presence of a foolish man, when thou perceivest not [in him] the lips of knowledge.
public_domain_references.brenton: All things are adverse to a foolish man; but wise lips are the weapons of discretion.

pob.text: The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way[b][a], but the folly of fools is deceit.

spob.text: A prudent person’s wisdom is understanding his own path. In contrast, the folly of fools is deceit.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The wisdom of the prudent is to discern his way, but the folly of fools deceives them.
public_domain_references.web: The wisdom of the prudent is to think about his way, but the folly of fools is deceit.
public_domain_references.asv: The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way; But the folly of fools is deceit.
public_domain_references.kjv: The wisdom of the prudent [is] to understand his way: but the folly of fools [is] deceit.
public_domain_references.brenton: The wisdom of the prudent will understand their ways; but the folly of fools leads astray.

pob.text: Fools mock guilt[b][a], but among the upright there is favor.

spob.text: Fools treat guilt as a joke,[a] but favor is found among those who do what is right.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Fools mock the making of amends, but goodwill is found among the upright.
public_domain_references.web: Fools mock at making atonement for sins, but among the upright there is good will.
public_domain_references.asv: A trespass-offering mocketh fools; But among the upright there is good will.
public_domain_references.kjv: Fools make a mock at sin: but among the righteous [there is] favour.
public_domain_references.brenton: The houses of transgressors will need purification; but the houses of the just are acceptable.

pob.text: The heart knows the bitterness of its soul[b][a], and no stranger shares in its joy.

spob.text: The heart knows its own bitterness, and no outsider can share its joy.

public_domain_references.bsb: The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger shares in its joy.
public_domain_references.web: The heart knows its own bitterness and joy; he will not share these with a stranger.
public_domain_references.asv: The heart knoweth its own bitterness; And a stranger doth not intermeddle with its joy.
public_domain_references.kjv: The heart knoweth his own bitterness; and a stranger doth not intermeddle with his joy.
public_domain_references.brenton: [If] a man's mind is intelligent, his soul is sorrowful; and when he rejoices, he has no fellowship with pride.

pob.text: The house of the wicked will be destroyed[a], but the tent of the upright will flourish.

spob.text: The house of people who do evil will be destroyed. But the tent of people who do what is right will flourish.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
public_domain_references.web: The house of the wicked will be overthrown, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
public_domain_references.asv: The house of the wicked shall be overthrown; But the tent of the upright shall flourish.
public_domain_references.kjv: The house of the wicked shall be overthrown: but the tabernacle of the upright shall flourish.
public_domain_references.brenton: The houses of ungodly men shall be utterly destroyed; but the tabernacles of them that walk uprightly shall stand.

pob.text: There is a way that seems right to a man[a], but its end is the ways of death.

spob.text: There is a way that seems right to a man, but in the end it leads down paths of death.

public_domain_references.bsb: There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death.
public_domain_references.web: There is a way which seems right to a man, but in the end it leads to death.
public_domain_references.asv: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man; But the end thereof are the ways of death.
public_domain_references.kjv: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof [are] the ways of death.
public_domain_references.brenton: There is a way which seems to be right with men, but the ends of it reach to the depth of hell.

pob.text: Even in laughter the heart may ache[b][a], and the end of joy is grief.

spob.text: Even while a person laughs, their heart may ache,[a] and joy ends in grief.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Even in laughter the heart may ache, and joy may end in sorrow.
public_domain_references.web: Even in laughter the heart may be sorrowful, and mirth may end in heaviness.
public_domain_references.asv: Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful; And the end of mirth is heaviness.
public_domain_references.kjv: Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful; and the end of that mirth [is] heaviness.
public_domain_references.brenton: Grief mingles not with mirth; and joy in the end comes to grief.

pob.text: The one who turns away in heart will be filled with his own ways[b][a], and a good man with what comes from himself.

spob.text: The one whose heart turns away will have his fill of what his own ways produce, and a good man will have his fill of what his own conduct produces.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The backslider in heart receives the fill of his own ways, but a good man is rewarded for his ways.
public_domain_references.web: The unfaithful will be repaid for his own ways; likewise a good man will be rewarded for his ways.
public_domain_references.asv: The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways; And a good man [shall be satisfied] from himself.
public_domain_references.kjv: The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways: and a good man [shall be satisfied] from himself.
public_domain_references.brenton: A stout-hearted [man] shall be filled with his own ways; and a good man with his own thoughts.

pob.text: A simple man believes every word[a], but a prudent man considers his steps.

spob.text: A naive person believes every word,[a] but a prudent person thinks carefully about the steps they take.

public_domain_references.bsb: The simple man believes every word, but the prudent man watches his steps.
public_domain_references.web: A simple man believes everything, but the prudent man carefully considers his ways.
public_domain_references.asv: The simple believeth every word; But the prudent man looketh well to his going.
public_domain_references.kjv: The simple believeth every word: but the prudent [man] looketh well to his going.
public_domain_references.brenton: The simple believes every word: but the prudent man betakes himself to after-thought.

pob.text: A wise man fears and turns away from evil[a], but a fool is reckless and confident.

spob.text: A wise man fears evil and turns away from it. But a fool acts recklessly[a], sure of himself.

public_domain_references.bsb: A wise man fears and turns from evil, but a fool is careless and reckless.
public_domain_references.web: A wise man fears and shuns evil, but the fool is hot headed and reckless.
public_domain_references.asv: A wise man feareth, and departeth from evil; But the fool beareth himself insolently, and is confident.
public_domain_references.kjv: A wise [man] feareth, and departeth from evil: but the fool rageth, and is confident.
public_domain_references.brenton: A wise man fears, and departs from evil; but the fool trusts in himself, and joins himself with the transgressor.

pob.text: A short-tempered man acts foolishly[b][a], and a man of schemes is hated.

spob.text: A short-tempered man does foolish things, and a man who schemes is hated.

public_domain_references.bsb: A quick-tempered man acts foolishly, and a devious man is hated.
public_domain_references.web: He who is quick to become angry will commit folly, and a crafty man is hated.
public_domain_references.asv: He that is soon angry will deal foolishly; And a man of wicked devices is hated.
public_domain_references.kjv: [He that is] soon angry dealeth foolishly: and a man of wicked devices is hated.
public_domain_references.brenton: A passionate man acts inconsiderately; but a sensible man bears up under many things.

pob.text: The simple inherit folly[a], but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.

spob.text: Those who are easily led inherit foolishness, but people with good judgment are crowned with knowledge.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
public_domain_references.web: The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
public_domain_references.asv: The simple inherit folly; But the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
public_domain_references.kjv: The simple inherit folly: but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
public_domain_references.brenton: Fools shall have mischief for their portion; but the prudent shall take fast hold of understanding.

pob.text: The evil bow down before the good[b][a], and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.

spob.text: Evil people bow low before good people, and wicked people are at the gates of a righteous person.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The evil bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
public_domain_references.web: The evil bow down before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
public_domain_references.asv: The evil bow down before the good; And the wicked, at the gates of the righteous.
public_domain_references.kjv: The evil bow before the good; and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
public_domain_references.brenton: Evil men shall fall before the good; and the ungodly shall attend at the gates of the righteous.

pob.text: Even his neighbor hates a poor man[b][a], but the friends of a rich man are many.

spob.text: Even a poor man’s neighbor[a] hates him, but many people attach themselves to a rich man.

public_domain_references.bsb: The poor man is hated even by his neighbor, but many are those who love the rich.
public_domain_references.web: The poor person is shunned even by his own neighbor, but the rich person has many friends.
public_domain_references.asv: The poor is hated even of his own neighbor; But the rich hath many friends.
public_domain_references.kjv: The poor is hated even of his own neighbour: but the rich [hath] many friends.
public_domain_references.brenton: Friends will hate poor friends; but the friends of the rich are many.

pob.text: Whoever despises his neighbor sins[a], but blessed is he who is gracious to the poor.

spob.text: Whoever looks down on a neighbor sins, but whoever shows kindness to the poor is blessed.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: He who despises his neighbor sins, but blessed is he who shows kindness to the poor.
public_domain_references.web: He who despises his neighbor sins, but he who has pity on the poor is blessed.
public_domain_references.asv: He that despiseth his neighbor sinneth; But he that hath pity on the poor, happy is he.
public_domain_references.kjv: He that despiseth his neighbour sinneth: but he that hath mercy on the poor, happy [is] he.
public_domain_references.brenton: He that dishonours the needy sins: but he that has pity on the poor is most blessed.

pob.text: Will not those who devise evil go astray? But steadfast love and faithfulness belong to those who devise good[a].

spob.text: Don’t those who plan evil go astray? But steadfast love and faithfulness belong to those who plan what is good.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Do not those who contrive evil go astray? But those who plan goodness find loving devotion and faithfulness.
public_domain_references.web: Don’t they go astray who plot evil? But love and faithfulness belong to those who plan good.
public_domain_references.asv: Do they not err that devise evil? But mercy and truth [shall be to] them that devise good.
public_domain_references.kjv: Do they not err that devise evil? but mercy and truth [shall be] to them that devise good.
public_domain_references.brenton: They that go astray devise evils: but the good devise mercy and truth. The framers of evil do not understand mercy and truth: but compassion and faithfulness are with the framers of good.

pob.text: In all labor there is profit[a], but mere talk leads only to lack.

spob.text: All hard work brings gain, but mere talk leads only to having too little.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: There is profit in all labor, but mere talk leads only to poverty.
public_domain_references.web: In all hard work there is profit, but the talk of the lips leads only to poverty.
public_domain_references.asv: In all labor there is profit; But the talk of the lips [tendeth] only to penury.
public_domain_references.kjv: In all labour there is profit: but the talk of the lips [tendeth] only to penury.
public_domain_references.brenton: With every one [who is] careful there is abundance: but the pleasure-taking and indolent shall be in want.

pob.text: The crown of the wise is their wealth[a], but the folly of fools is folly.

spob.text: For wise people, wealth is a crown of honor; but fools are marked by foolishness.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The crown of the wise is their wealth, but the effort of fools is folly.
public_domain_references.web: The crown of the wise is their riches, but the folly of fools crowns them with folly.
public_domain_references.asv: The crown of the wise is their riches; [But] the folly of fools is [only] folly.
public_domain_references.kjv: The crown of the wise [is] their riches: [but] the foolishness of fools [is] folly.
public_domain_references.brenton: A prudent man is the crown of the wise: but the occupation of fools is evil.

pob.text: A truthful witness rescues lives[c][b][a], but one who breathes out lies is deceitful.

spob.text: A witness who tells the truth rescues lives, but one who speaks lies is deceitful.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: A truthful witness saves lives, but one who utters lies is deceitful.
public_domain_references.web: A truthful witness saves souls, but a false witness is deceitful.
public_domain_references.asv: A true witness delivereth souls; But he that uttereth lies [causeth] deceit.
public_domain_references.kjv: A true witness delivereth souls: but a deceitful [witness] speaketh lies.
public_domain_references.brenton: A faithful witness shall deliver a soul from evil: but a deceitful [man] kindles falsehoods.

pob.text: In the fear of Yahweh there is strong confidence[a], and for his children there will be a refuge.

spob.text: A person who lives in reverent fear of Yahweh has firm confidence, and there will be a refuge for that person’s children.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: He who fears the LORD is secure in confidence, and his children shall have a place of refuge.
public_domain_references.web: In the fear of Yahweh is a secure fortress, and he will be a refuge for his children.
public_domain_references.asv: In the fear of Jehovah is strong confidence; And his children shall have a place of refuge.
public_domain_references.kjv: In the fear of the LORD [is] strong confidence: and his children shall have a place of refuge.
public_domain_references.brenton: In the fear of the Lord is strong confidence: and he leaves his children a support.

pob.text: The fear of Yahweh is a fountain of life[b][a], to turn one away from the snares of death.

spob.text: Fear of Yahweh[a] is a life-giving fountain. This fear turns a person away from the traps of death.

public_domain_references.bsb: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a man from the snares of death.
public_domain_references.web: The fear of Yahweh is a fountain of life, turning people from the snares of death.
public_domain_references.asv: The fear of Jehovah is a fountain of life, That one may depart from the snares of death.
public_domain_references.kjv: The fear of the LORD [is] a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death.
public_domain_references.brenton: The commandment of the Lord is a fountain of life; and it causes [men] to turn aside from the snare of death.

pob.text: In a multitude of people is a king’s splendor[a], but without people, a ruler’s ruin.

spob.text: A king gains honor from having many people, but without people, a ruler comes to ruin.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: A large population is a king’s splendor, but a lack of subjects is a prince’s ruin.
public_domain_references.web: In the multitude of people is the king’s glory, but in the lack of people is the destruction of the prince.
public_domain_references.asv: In the multitude of people is the king’s glory; But in the want of people is the destruction of the prince.
public_domain_references.kjv: In the multitude of people [is] the king’s honour: but in the want of people [is] the destruction of the prince.
public_domain_references.brenton: In a populous nation is the glory of a king: but in the failure of people is the ruin of a prince.

pob.text: One who is slow to anger has great understanding[a], but one who is quick-tempered exalts folly.

spob.text: People who are slow to become angry have great understanding, but people with a quick temper put foolishness on display.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: A patient man has great understanding, but a quick-tempered man promotes folly.
public_domain_references.web: He who is slow to anger has great understanding, but he who has a quick temper displays folly.
public_domain_references.asv: He that is slow to anger is of great understanding; But he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.
public_domain_references.kjv: [He that is] slow to wrath [is] of great understanding: but [he that is] hasty of spirit exalteth folly.
public_domain_references.brenton: A man slow to wrath abounds in wisdom: but a man of impatient spirit is very foolish.

pob.text: A tranquil heart is life to the body[b][a], but jealousy is rottenness to the bones.

spob.text: A calm heart gives life to the body,[a] but jealousy[b] rots the bones.

public_domain_references.bsb: A tranquil heart is life to the body, but envy rots the bones.
public_domain_references.web: The life of the body is a heart at peace, but envy rots the bones.
public_domain_references.asv: A tranquil heart is the life of the flesh; But envy is the rottenness of the bones.
public_domain_references.kjv: A sound heart [is] the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones.
public_domain_references.brenton: A meek-spirited man is a healer of the heart: but a sensitive heart is a corruption of the bones.

pob.text: Whoever oppresses the poor insults his Maker[a], but whoever is gracious to the needy honors him.

spob.text: Anyone who exploits the poor insults the God who made them, but anyone who shows kindness to people in need honors God.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Whoever oppresses the poor taunts their Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors Him.
public_domain_references.web: He who oppresses the poor shows contempt for his Maker, but he who is kind to the needy honors him.
public_domain_references.asv: He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker; But he that hath mercy on the needy honoreth him.
public_domain_references.kjv: He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker: but he that honoureth him hath mercy on the poor.
public_domain_references.brenton: He that oppresses the needy provokes his Maker: but he that honours him has pity upon the poor.

pob.text: By his evil the wicked is driven away[c][b][a], but the righteous finds refuge in his death.

spob.text: The wicked man’s evil brings him down,[a] but the righteous person finds refuge at his death.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: The wicked man is thrown down by his own sin, but the righteous man has a refuge even in death.
public_domain_references.web: The wicked is brought down in his calamity, but in death, the righteous has a refuge.

public_domain_references.kjv: The wicked is driven away in his wickedness: but the righteous hath hope in his death.
