public_domain_references.bsb: A rich man’s wealth is his fortified city; it is like a high wall in his imagination.
public_domain_references.web: The rich man’s wealth is his strong city, like an unscalable wall in his own imagination.
public_domain_references.asv: The rich man’s wealth is his strong city, And as a high wall in his own imagination.
public_domain_references.kjv: The rich man’s wealth [is] his strong city, and as an high wall in his own conceit.
public_domain_references.brenton: The wealth of a rich man is a strong city; and its glory casts a broad shadow.

pob.text: Before destruction a man's heart is haughty[a], and before honor comes humility.

spob.text: A man's[a] heart rises with pride before destruction, but humility comes before honor.

public_domain_references.bsb: Before his downfall a man’s heart is proud, but humility comes before honor.
public_domain_references.web: Before destruction the heart of man is proud, but before honor is humility.
public_domain_references.asv: Before destruction the heart of man is haughty; And before honor [goeth] humility.
public_domain_references.kjv: Before destruction the heart of man is haughty, and before honour [is] humility.
public_domain_references.brenton: Before ruin a man's heart is exalted, and before honour it is humble.

pob.text: He who answers a matter before he hears it[a], it is folly and shame to him.

spob.text: Whoever answers before hearing the matter acts foolishly and brings shame on himself.

public_domain_references.bsb: He who answers a matter before he hears it— this is folly and disgrace to him.
public_domain_references.web: He who answers before he hears, that is folly and shame to him.
public_domain_references.asv: He that giveth answer before he heareth, It is folly and shame unto him.
public_domain_references.kjv: He that answereth a matter before he heareth [it], it [is] folly and shame unto him.
public_domain_references.brenton: Whoso answers a word before he hears [a cause], it is folly and reproach to him.

pob.text: A man's spirit can sustain him in sickness[b][a], but a crushed spirit—who can bear it?

spob.text: A person's spirit can carry them through illness. But who can endure a crushed spirit?

public_domain_references.bsb: The spirit of a man can endure his sickness, but who can survive a broken spirit?
public_domain_references.web: A man’s spirit will sustain him in sickness, but a crushed spirit, who can bear?
public_domain_references.asv: The spirit of a man will sustain his infirmity; But a broken spirit who can bear?
public_domain_references.kjv: The spirit of a man will sustain his infirmity; but a wounded spirit who can bear?
public_domain_references.brenton: A wise servant calms a man's anger; but who can endure a faint-hearted man?

pob.text: An understanding heart acquires knowledge[b][a], and the ear of the wise seeks knowledge.

spob.text: A heart that understands gains knowledge, and wise people listen for knowledge.

public_domain_references.bsb: The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks it out.
public_domain_references.web: The heart of the discerning gets knowledge. The ear of the wise seeks knowledge.
public_domain_references.asv: The heart of the prudent getteth knowledge; And the ear of the wise seeketh knowledge.
public_domain_references.kjv: The heart of the prudent getteth knowledge; and the ear of the wise seeketh knowledge.
public_domain_references.brenton: The heart of the sensible [man] purchases discretion; and the ears of the wise seek understanding.

pob.text: A man's gift makes room for him[b][a], and brings him before great men.

spob.text: A person’s gift makes room for them and brings them into the presence of important people.

public_domain_references.bsb: A man’s gift opens doors for him, and brings him before great men.
public_domain_references.web: A man’s gift makes room for him, and brings him before great men.
public_domain_references.asv: A man’s gift maketh room for him, And bringeth him before great men.
public_domain_references.kjv: A man’s gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.
public_domain_references.brenton: A man's gift enlarges him, and seats him among princes.

pob.text: The first to present his case seems right[a], until his neighbor comes and examines him.

spob.text: The first person to tell his side of a dispute seems right—until the other person involved comes and questions him closely.

public_domain_references.bsb: The first to state his case seems right until another comes and cross-examines him.
public_domain_references.web: He who pleads his cause first seems right— until another comes and questions him.
public_domain_references.asv: He that pleadeth his cause first [seemeth] just; But his neighbor cometh and searcheth him out.
public_domain_references.kjv: [He that is] first in his own cause [seemeth] just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him.
public_domain_references.brenton: A righteous man accuses himself at the beginning of his speech, but when he has entered upon the attack, the adversary is reproved.

pob.text: The lot puts an end to disputes[a], and separates between the mighty.

spob.text: Casting lots puts an end to disputes and decides between powerful opponents.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Casting the lot ends quarrels and separates strong opponents.
public_domain_references.web: The lot settles disputes, and keeps strong ones apart.
public_domain_references.asv: The lot causeth contentions to cease, And parteth between the mighty.
public_domain_references.kjv: The lot causeth contentions to cease, and parteth between the mighty.
public_domain_references.brenton: A silent [man] quells strifes, and determines between great powers.

pob.text: A brother offended is harder to win than a fortified city[b][a], and quarrels are like the bars of a citadel.

spob.text: A brother who has been offended is harder to win back than a fortified city. Quarrels are like the bars that lock a citadel.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: An offended brother is harder to win than a fortified city, and disputes are like the bars of a castle.
public_domain_references.web: A brother offended is more difficult than a fortified city. Disputes are like the bars of a fortress.
public_domain_references.asv: A brother offended [is harder to be won] than a strong city; And [such] contentions are like the bars of a castle.
public_domain_references.kjv: A brother offended [is harder to be won] than a strong city: and [their] contentions [are] like the bars of a castle.
public_domain_references.brenton: A brother helped by a brother is as a strong and high city; and is [as] strong as a [well]-founded palace.

pob.text: From the fruit of a man's mouth his stomach is satisfied[a]; he is satisfied by the produce of his lips.

spob.text: A man is satisfied by the results of his words; he is satisfied by what his lips produce.

public_domain_references.bsb: From the fruit of his mouth a man’s belly is filled; with the harvest from his lips he is satisfied.
public_domain_references.web: A man’s stomach is filled with the fruit of his mouth. With the harvest of his lips he is satisfied.
public_domain_references.asv: A man’s belly shall be filled with the fruit of his mouth; With the increase of his lips shall he be satisfied.
public_domain_references.kjv: A man’s belly shall be satisfied with the fruit of his mouth; [and] with the increase of his lips shall he be filled.
public_domain_references.brenton: A man fills his belly with the fruits of his mouth; and he shall be satisfied with the fruits of his lips.

pob.text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue[b][a], and those who love it will eat its fruit.

spob.text: The tongue can bring death or life. Those who love it will eat the fruit it produces.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Life and death are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
public_domain_references.web: Death and life are in the power of the tongue; those who love it will eat its fruit.
public_domain_references.asv: Death and life are in the power of the tongue; And they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.
public_domain_references.kjv: Death and life [are] in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.
public_domain_references.brenton: Life and death are in the power of the tongue; and they that rule it shall eat the fruits thereof.

pob.text: He who finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from Yahweh[a].

spob.text: A man who finds a wife finds something good and receives favor from Yahweh.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: He who finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from the LORD.
public_domain_references.web: Whoever finds a wife finds a good thing, and obtains favor of Yahweh.
public_domain_references.asv: Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing, And obtaineth favor of Jehovah.
public_domain_references.kjv: [Whoso] findeth a wife findeth a good [thing], and obtaineth favour of the LORD.
public_domain_references.brenton: He that has found a good wife has found favours, and has received gladness from God.

pob.text: The poor man speaks with pleas[a], but the rich man answers harshly.

spob.text: A poor man pleads, but a rich man answers harshly.

public_domain_references.bsb: The poor man pleads for mercy, but the rich man answers harshly.
public_domain_references.web: The poor plead for mercy, but the rich answer harshly.
public_domain_references.asv: The poor useth entreaties; But the rich answereth roughly.
public_domain_references.kjv: The poor useth intreaties; but the rich answereth roughly.

pob.text: A man of many companions may come to ruin[a], but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.

spob.text: A man can have many companions and still come to ruin, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: A man of many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who stays closer than a brother.
public_domain_references.web: A man of many companions may be ruined, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
public_domain_references.asv: He that maketh many friends [doeth it] to his own destruction; But there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.
public_domain_references.kjv: A man [that hath] friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend [that] sticketh closer than a brother.

pob.text: Better is a poor man who walks in his integrity than one who is crooked in his speech and is a fool[a][b].

spob.text: It is better to be poor and walk through life with integrity than to be a fool who speaks crooked words.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Better a poor man who walks with integrity than a fool whose lips are perverse.
public_domain_references.web: Better is the poor who walks in his integrity than he who is perverse in his lips and is a fool.
public_domain_references.asv: Better is the poor that walketh in his integrity Than he that is perverse in his lips and is a fool.
public_domain_references.kjv: Better [is] the poor that walketh in his integrity, than [he that is] perverse in his lips, and is a fool.

pob.text: Also[a], without knowledge, desire is not good, and whoever hurries with his feet sins.

spob.text: Also, desire[a] without knowledge is not good. Whoever rushes ahead with their feet sins.

public_domain_references.bsb: Even zeal is no good without knowledge, and he who hurries his footsteps misses the mark.
public_domain_references.web: It isn’t good to have zeal without knowledge, nor to be hasty with one’s feet and miss the way.
public_domain_references.asv: Also, that the soul be without knowledge is not good; And he that hasteth with his feet sinneth.
public_domain_references.kjv: Also, [that] the soul [be] without knowledge, [it is] not good; and he that hasteth with [his] feet sinneth.

pob.text: A man's folly ruins his way[b][a], and his heart rages against Yahweh.

spob.text: A man's[a] foolishness ruins the path of his life, and his heart rages against Yahweh.

public_domain_references.bsb: A man’s own folly subverts his way, yet his heart rages against the LORD.
public_domain_references.web: The foolishness of man subverts his way; his heart rages against Yahweh.
public_domain_references.asv: The foolishness of man subverteth his way; And his heart fretteth against Jehovah.
public_domain_references.kjv: The foolishness of man perverteth his way: and his heart fretteth against the LORD.
public_domain_references.brenton: The folly of a man spoils his ways: and he blames God in his heart.

pob.text: Wealth adds many friends[a], but a poor man is separated from his friend.

spob.text: Wealth brings many friends, but a poor man ends up cut off from his friend.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Wealth attracts many friends, but a poor man is deserted by his friend.
public_domain_references.web: Wealth adds many friends, but the poor is separated from his friend.
public_domain_references.asv: Wealth addeth many friends; But the poor is separated from his friend.
public_domain_references.kjv: Wealth maketh many friends; but the poor is separated from his neighbour.
public_domain_references.brenton: Wealth acquires many friends; but the poor is deserted even of the friend he has.

pob.text: A false witness will not go unpunished[b][a], and one who breathes out lies will not escape.

spob.text: Anyone who gives false testimony will be punished. Whoever tells lies will not escape.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who utters lies will not escape.
public_domain_references.web: A false witness shall not be unpunished. He who pours out lies shall not go free.
public_domain_references.asv: A false witness shall not be unpunished; And he that uttereth lies shall not escape.
public_domain_references.kjv: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and [he that] speaketh lies shall not escape.
public_domain_references.brenton: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that accuses unjustly shall not escape.

pob.text: Many seek the favor of a noble man[b][a], and everyone is a friend to a man who gives gifts.

spob.text: Many people try to win favor with a generous man, and everyone befriends a man who gives gifts.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Many seek the favor of the prince, and everyone is a friend of the gift giver.
public_domain_references.web: Many will entreat the favor of a ruler, and everyone is a friend to a man who gives gifts.
public_domain_references.asv: Many will entreat the favor of the liberal man; And every man is a friend to him that giveth gifts.
public_domain_references.kjv: Many will intreat the favour of the prince: and every man [is] a friend to him that giveth gifts.
public_domain_references.brenton: Many court the favour of kings; but every bad man becomes a reproach to [another] man.

pob.text: All the brothers of a poor man hate him[a]; how much more do his friends keep far from him! He pursues words[b], but they are not there.

spob.text: All of a poor man's brothers[a] hate him. His friends stay even farther away! He chases after words, but they are not there.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: All the brothers of a poor man hate him— how much more do his friends avoid him! He may pursue them with pleading, but they are nowhere to be found.
public_domain_references.web: All the relatives of the poor shun him; how much more do his friends avoid him! He pursues them with pleas, but they are gone.
public_domain_references.asv: All the brethren of the poor do hate him: How much more do his friends go far from him! He pursueth [them with] words, [but] they are gone.
public_domain_references.kjv: All the brethren of the poor do hate him: how much more do his friends go far from him? he pursueth [them with] words, [yet] they [are] wanting [to him].
public_domain_references.brenton: Every one who hates [his] poor brother shall also be far from friendship. Good understanding will draw near to them that know it, and a sensible man will find it. He that does much harm perfects mischief; and he that uses provoking words shall not escape.

pob.text: Whoever gains sense loves his own life[b][a]; whoever keeps understanding will find good.

spob.text: Those who gain good sense love their own lives; those who hold on to understanding will find what is good.

public_domain_references.bsb: He who acquires wisdom loves himself; one who safeguards understanding will find success.
public_domain_references.web: He who gets wisdom loves his own soul. He who keeps understanding shall find good.
public_domain_references.asv: He that getteth wisdom loveth his own soul: He that keepeth understanding shall find good.
public_domain_references.kjv: He that getteth wisdom loveth his own soul: he that keepeth understanding shall find good.
public_domain_references.brenton: He that procures wisdom loves himself; and he that keeps wisdom shall find good.

pob.text: A false witness will not go unpunished[b][a], and one who breathes out lies will perish.

spob.text: A witness who lies will not escape punishment. A person who pours out lies as easily as breathing will perish.

public_domain_references.bsb: A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who pours out lies will perish.
public_domain_references.web: A false witness shall not be unpunished. He who utters lies shall perish.
public_domain_references.asv: A false witness shall not be unpunished; And he that uttereth lies shall perish.
public_domain_references.kjv: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and [he that] speaketh lies shall perish.
public_domain_references.brenton: A false witness shall not be unpunished; and whosoever shall kindle mischief shall perish by it.

pob.text: Luxury is not fitting for a fool[c][b][a], much less for a slave to rule over princes.

spob.text: A life of luxury does not suit a fool. It is even less fitting for a slave[a] to rule over princes.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Luxury is unseemly for a fool— how much worse for a slave to rule over princes!
public_domain_references.web: Delicate living is not appropriate for a fool, much less for a servant to have rule over princes.
public_domain_references.asv: Delicate living is not seemly for a fool; Much less for a servant to have rule over princes.
public_domain_references.kjv: Delight is not seemly for a fool; much less for a servant to have rule over princes.
public_domain_references.brenton: Delight does not suit a fool, nor [is it seemly] if a servant should begin to rule with haughtiness.

pob.text: A man's insight makes him slow to anger[b][a], and it is his glory to overlook an offense.

spob.text: Good sense makes a man slow to anger.[a] It is honorable to overlook an offense.

public_domain_references.bsb: A man’s insight gives him patience, and his virtue is to overlook an offense.
public_domain_references.web: The discretion of a man makes him slow to anger. It is his glory to overlook an offense.
public_domain_references.asv: The discretion of a man maketh him slow to anger; And it is his glory to pass over a transgression.
public_domain_references.kjv: The discretion of a man deferreth his anger; and [it is] his glory to pass over a transgression.
public_domain_references.brenton: A merciful man is long-suffering; and his triumph overtakes transgressors.

pob.text: A king’s wrath is like the growling of a young lion[b][a], but his favor is like dew on the grass.

spob.text: A king’s fierce anger is like a young lion’s growl, but his favor is like dew that refreshes the grass.

public_domain_references.bsb: A king’s rage is like the roar of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.
public_domain_references.web: The king’s wrath is like the roaring of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.
public_domain_references.asv: The king’s wrath is as the roaring of a lion; But his favor is as dew upon the grass.
public_domain_references.kjv: The king’s wrath [is] as the roaring of a lion; but his favour [is] as dew upon the grass.
public_domain_references.brenton: The threatening of a king is like the roaring of a lion; but as dew on the grass, so is his favour.

pob.text: A foolish son is ruin to his father[a], and a wife’s quarrels are a continual dripping.

spob.text: A foolish son brings ruin on his father, and a wife’s quarrels are like a leak that never stops dripping.

public_domain_references.bsb: A foolish son is his father’s ruin, and a quarrelsome wife is like a constant dripping.
public_domain_references.web: A foolish son is the calamity of his father. A wife’s quarrels are a continual dripping.
public_domain_references.asv: A foolish son is the calamity of his father; And the contentions of a wife are a continual dropping.
public_domain_references.kjv: A foolish son [is] the calamity of his father: and the contentions of a wife [are] a continual dropping.
public_domain_references.brenton: A foolish son is a disgrace to his father: vows [paid out] of the hire of a harlot are not pure.

pob.text: A house and wealth are an inheritance from fathers[a], but a prudent wife is from Yahweh.

spob.text: A house and wealth are inherited from fathers, but a wife with good judgment comes from Yahweh.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Houses and wealth are inherited from fathers, but a prudent wife is from the LORD.
public_domain_references.web: House and riches are an inheritance from fathers, but a prudent wife is from Yahweh.
public_domain_references.asv: House and riches are an inheritance from fathers; But a prudent wife is from Jehovah.
public_domain_references.kjv: House and riches [are] the inheritance of fathers: and a prudent wife [is] from the LORD.
public_domain_references.brenton: Fathers divide house and substance to [their] children: but a wife is suited to a man by the Lord.

pob.text: Laziness brings on deep sleep[b][a], and a slack person will go hungry.

spob.text: Laziness makes a person sink into deep sleep, and a negligent person will go hungry.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Laziness brings on deep sleep, and an idle soul will suffer hunger.
public_domain_references.web: Slothfulness casts into a deep sleep. The idle soul shall suffer hunger.
public_domain_references.asv: Slothfulness casteth into a deep sleep; And the idle soul shall suffer hunger.
public_domain_references.kjv: Slothfulness casteth into a deep sleep; and an idle soul shall suffer hunger.
public_domain_references.brenton: Cowardice possesses the effeminate [man]; and the soul of the sluggard shall hunger.

pob.text: Whoever keeps the commandment keeps his life[b][a]; he who despises his ways will die.

spob.text: Whoever obeys the commandment protects his life, but whoever has no regard for his own conduct[a] will die.

public_domain_references.bsb: He who keeps a commandment preserves his soul, but he who is careless in his ways will die.
public_domain_references.web: He who keeps the commandment keeps his soul, but he who is contemptuous in his ways shall die.
public_domain_references.asv: He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his soul; [But] he that is careless of his ways shall die.
public_domain_references.kjv: He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his own soul; [but] he that despiseth his ways shall die.
public_domain_references.brenton: He that keeps the commandment keeps his own soul; but he that despises his ways shall perish.

pob.text: Whoever is gracious to the poor lends to Yahweh[a], and he will repay him for his deed.

spob.text: Whoever shows grace to the poor lends to Yahweh. Yahweh will repay that person for what they have done.

public_domain_references.bsb: Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender.
public_domain_references.web: He who has pity on the poor lends to Yahweh; he will reward him.
public_domain_references.asv: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Jehovah, And his good deed will he pay him again.
public_domain_references.kjv: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the LORD; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.
public_domain_references.brenton: He that has pity on the poor lends to the Lord; and he will recompense to him according to his gift.

pob.text: Discipline your son[a], for there is hope[b]; do not set your heart on putting him to death.

spob.text: Discipline your son, because there is hope for him.[a] But do not make his death your goal.

public_domain_references.bsb: Discipline your son, for in that there is hope; do not be party to his death.
public_domain_references.web: Discipline your son, for there is hope; don’t be a willing party to his death.
public_domain_references.asv: Chasten thy son, seeing there is hope; And set not thy heart on his destruction.
public_domain_references.kjv: Chasten thy son while there is hope, and let not thy soul spare for his crying.
public_domain_references.brenton: Chasten thy son, for so he shall be hopeful; and be not exalted in thy soul to haughtiness.

pob.text: A hot-tempered man bears the penalty[a], for if you rescue him, you will only have to do it again.

spob.text: A hot-tempered person pays the penalty for his anger. If you rescue him, you will only have to rescue him again.

public_domain_references.bsb: A man of great anger must pay the penalty; if you rescue him, you will have to do so again.
public_domain_references.web: A hot-tempered man must pay the penalty, for if you rescue him, you must do it again.
public_domain_references.asv: A man of great wrath shall bear the penalty; For if thou deliver [him], thou must do it yet again.
public_domain_references.kjv: A man of great wrath shall suffer punishment: for if thou deliver [him], yet thou must do it again.
public_domain_references.brenton: A malicious man shall be severely punished, and if he commit injury, he shall also lose his life.

pob.text: Listen to counsel and accept discipline[a], so that you may become wise in the end.

spob.text: Listen to guidance and accept discipline, so that you may become wise in the future.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Listen to counsel and accept discipline, that you may be wise the rest of your days.
public_domain_references.web: Listen to counsel and receive instruction, that you may be wise in your latter end.
public_domain_references.asv: Hear counsel, and receive instruction, That thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.
public_domain_references.kjv: Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.
public_domain_references.brenton: Hear, son, the instruction of thy father, that thou mayest be wise at thy latter end.

pob.text: Many are the plans in a man's heart[a], but the counsel of Yahweh will stand.

spob.text: A man may have many plans in his heart, but Yahweh’s purpose will stand.

public_domain_references.bsb: Many plans are in a man’s heart, but the purpose of the LORD will prevail.
public_domain_references.web: There are many plans in a man’s heart, but Yahweh’s counsel will prevail.
public_domain_references.asv: There are many devices in a man’s heart; But the counsel of Jehovah, that shall stand.
public_domain_references.kjv: [There are] many devices in a man’s heart; nevertheless the counsel of the LORD, that shall stand.
public_domain_references.brenton: [There are] many thoughts in a man's heart; but the counsel of the Lord abides for ever.

pob.text: What is desired in a man is his steadfast love[b][a], and a poor man is better than a liar.

spob.text: What people value in a man is his faithful love,[a][b] and a poor man is better than a liar.

public_domain_references.bsb: The desire of a man is loving devotion; better to be poor than a liar.
public_domain_references.web: That which makes a man to be desired is his kindness. A poor man is better than a liar.
public_domain_references.asv: That which maketh a man to be desired is his kindness; And a poor man is better than a liar.
public_domain_references.kjv: The desire of a man [is] his kindness: and a poor man [is] better than a liar.
public_domain_references.brenton: Mercy is a fruit to a man: and a poor man is better than a rich liar.

pob.text: The fear of Yahweh leads to life[a], and whoever has it will rest satisfied[c][b]; he will not be visited by harm.

spob.text: The fear of Yahweh leads to life. Whoever has this fear will rest content, and harm will not come upon them.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The fear of the LORD leads to life, that one may rest content, without visitation from harm.

public_domain_references.kjv: The thoughts of the diligent [tend] only to plenteousness; but of every one [that is] hasty only to want.

public_domain_references.brenton: To the froward God sends froward ways; for his works are pure and right.

public_domain_references.kjv: [As] coals [are] to burning coals, and wood to fire; so [is] a contentious man to kindle strife.
public_domain_references.brenton: A hearth for coals, and wood for fire; and a railing man for the tumult of strife.

pob.text: The words of a whisperer are like delicious morsels[b][a], and they go down into the inner chambers of the belly.

spob.text: Whispered gossip is like delicious bites.[a] It goes down into the belly and sinks deep within a person.

public_domain_references.bsb: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels that go down into the inmost being.

public_domain_references.kjv: The words of a talebearer [are] as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.
public_domain_references.brenton: The words of cunning knaves are soft; but they smite [even] to the inmost parts of the bowels.

pob.text: Like silver dross overlaid on earthenware are fervent lips with an evil heart[a].

spob.text: Warm, eager words on the lips of someone with an evil heart are like worthless silver residue coating a clay pot.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Like glaze covering an earthen vessel are burning lips and a wicked heart.
public_domain_references.web: Like silver dross on an earthen vessel are the lips of a fervent one with an evil heart.

public_domain_references.brenton: Silver dishonestly given is to be considered as a potsherd: smooth lips cover a grievous heart.

pob.text: A hater disguises himself with his lips[b][a], but within himself he sets deceit.

public_domain_references.web: A malicious man disguises himself with his lips, but he harbors evil in his heart.

public_domain_references.kjv: He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him;
public_domain_references.brenton: A weeping enemy promises all things with his lips, but in his heart he contrives deceit.

pob.text: When he makes his voice gracious[a], do not trust him[b], for seven abominations are in his heart.

spob.text: When he makes his voice sound kind, do not trust him, because seven[a] detestable things are in his heart.

public_domain_references.brenton: Though [thine] enemy intreat thee with a loud voice, consent not: for there are seven abominations in his heart.

pob.text: Whoever digs a pit will fall into it[a], and he who rolls a stone, it will come back on him.

public_domain_references.kjv: She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing [is] silk and purple.
public_domain_references.brenton: She makes for her husband clothes of double texture, and garments for herself of fine linen and scarlet.

pob.text: Her husband is known in the gates[b][a], when he sits among the elders of the land.

spob.text: Her husband is known at the city gates,[a] when he sits among the elders of the land.

public_domain_references.bsb: Her husband is known at the city gate, where he sits among the elders of the land.
public_domain_references.web: Her husband is respected in the gates, when he sits among the elders of the land.
public_domain_references.asv: Her husband is known in the gates, When he sitteth among the elders of the land.
public_domain_references.kjv: Her husband is known in the gates, when he sitteth among the elders of the land.
public_domain_references.brenton: And her husband becomes a distinguished [person] in the gates, when he sits in council with the old inhabitants of the land.

pob.text: She makes linen garments and sells them[c][b][a], and supplies belts to the merchant.

spob.text: She makes linen garments[a] and sells them. She also supplies belts[b] to a merchant.[c]

public_domain_references.bsb: She makes linen garments and sells them; she delivers sashes to the merchants.
public_domain_references.web: She makes linen garments and sells them, and delivers sashes to the merchant.
public_domain_references.asv: She maketh linen garments and selleth them, And delivereth girdles unto the merchant.
public_domain_references.kjv: She maketh fine linen, and selleth [it;] and delivereth girdles unto the merchant.
public_domain_references.brenton: She makes fine linens, and sells girdles to the Chananites: she opens her mouth heedfully and with propriety, and controls her tongue.

pob.text: Strength and dignity are her clothing[a], and she laughs at the days to come.

spob.text: She wears strength and dignity like clothing, and she laughs at the days ahead.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Strength and honor are her clothing, and she can laugh at the days to come.
public_domain_references.web: Strength and dignity are her clothing. She laughs at the time to come.
public_domain_references.asv: Strength and dignity are her clothing; And she laugheth at the time to come.
public_domain_references.kjv: Strength and honour [are] her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.
public_domain_references.brenton: She puts on strength and honour; and rejoices in the last days.

pob.text: She opens her mouth with wisdom[b][a], and the instruction of kindness is on her tongue.

spob.text: When she opens her mouth, she speaks with wisdom, and her tongue is ready to give kind instruction.[a][b]

public_domain_references.bsb: She opens her mouth with wisdom, and faithful instruction is on her tongue.
public_domain_references.web: She opens her mouth with wisdom. Kind instruction is on her tongue.
public_domain_references.asv: She openeth her mouth with wisdom; And the law of kindness is on her tongue.
public_domain_references.kjv: She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue [is] the law of kindness.
public_domain_references.brenton: The ways of her household are careful, and she eats not the bread of idleness.

pob.text: She watches over the ways of her household[b][a], and does not eat the bread of idleness.

spob.text: She carefully watches over the affairs of her household, and she does not live lazily.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: She watches over the affairs of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness.
public_domain_references.web: She looks well to the ways of her household, and doesn’t eat the bread of idleness.
public_domain_references.asv: She looketh well to the ways of her household, And eateth not the bread of idleness.
public_domain_references.kjv: She looketh well to the ways of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness.
public_domain_references.brenton: But she opens her mouth wisely, and according to law.

pob.text: Her children rise up and call her blessed[a]; her husband also[b], and he praises her:

spob.text: Her children[a] rise to honor her and declare that she is blessed. Her husband also praises her:

public_domain_references.bsb: Her children rise up and call her blessed; her husband praises her as well:
public_domain_references.web: Her children rise up and call her blessed. Her husband also praises her:
public_domain_references.asv: Her children rise up, and call her blessed; Her husband [also], and he praiseth her, [saying]:
public_domain_references.kjv: Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband [also], and he praiseth her.
public_domain_references.brenton: And [her] kindness to them sets up her children for them, and they grow rich, and her husband praises her.

pob.text: Many daughters have done nobly[b][a], but you surpass them all.

spob.text: Many women have shown strength and excellence, but you surpass them all.

public_domain_references.bsb: “Many daughters have done noble things, but you surpass them all!”
public_domain_references.web: “Many women do noble things, but you excel them all.”
public_domain_references.asv: Many daughters have done worthily, But thou excellest them all.
public_domain_references.kjv: Many daughters have done virtuously, but thou excellest them all.
public_domain_references.brenton: Many daughters have obtained wealth, many have wrought valiantly; but thou hast exceeded, thou hast surpassed all.

pob.text: Charm is deceitful[a], and beauty is fleeting[c][b], but a woman who fears Yahweh shall be praised.

spob.text: Charm is deceptive, and beauty fades away,[a] but a woman[b] who fears Yahweh will be praised.[c]

public_domain_references.bsb: Charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.
public_domain_references.web: Charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain; but a woman who fears Yahweh, she shall be praised.
public_domain_references.asv: Grace is deceitful, and beauty is vain; [But] a woman that feareth Jehovah, she shall be praised.
public_domain_references.kjv: Favour [is] deceitful, and beauty [is] vain: [but] a woman [that] feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.
public_domain_references.brenton: Charms are false, and woman's beauty is vain: for it is a wise woman that is blessed, and let her praise the fear of the Lord.

pob.text: Give her of the fruit of her hands[b][a], and let her works praise her in the gates.

spob.text: Give her a share of what her own hands have produced. Let her deeds themselves praise her publicly at the city gates.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Give her the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her at the gates.
public_domain_references.web: Give her of the fruit of her hands! Let her works praise her in the gates!
public_domain_references.asv: Give her of the fruit of her hands; And let her works praise her in the gates.
public_domain_references.kjv: Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works praise her in the gates.
public_domain_references.brenton: Give her of the fruit of her lips; and let her husband be praised in the gates.
